def: A user-driven profile lets an end user unbox a device, sign in with their own Microsoft Entra ID account, and finish provisioning themselves. A self-deploying profile needs no user interaction at all and authenticates the device itself, commonly for kiosks or shared devices. A pre-provisioned (white glove) profile lets a partner or IT do the time-consuming steps in advance, so the end user only completes a short final phase.
eg: Self-deploying profiles require a TPM 2.0 device that can authenticate on its own, since there is no user present to sign in and prove identity. Whichever profile is used, the Enrollment Status Page (ESP) is what actually blocks the desktop until provisioning finishes.

term: Windows Autopilot device preparation vs classic Autopilot
def: Windows Autopilot device preparation is the newer, streamlined cloud-native provisioning path, built for speed and simplified Entra-joined deployment with tighter Intune integration. Classic Autopilot deployment profiles (user-driven, self-deploying, pre-provisioned) remain available for hybrid Entra join and scenarios device preparation does not yet cover.
eg: Device preparation is Microsoft's direction going forward, but it currently only supports Microsoft Entra joined devices, not hybrid Entra join, so classic profiles still matter for hybrid environments.

def: A Windows 365 policy that defines how each Cloud PC is created: which Microsoft Entra ID group receives it, the image used, the Entra join type (Microsoft Entra joined or hybrid Entra joined), and the domain join configuration. It is what actually triggers Cloud PC creation once a user is licensed and assigned.
eg: A user needs both a Windows 365 license assignment and a matching provisioning policy scope; having only one of the two never results in a Cloud PC being created.

def: Windows 365 Enterprise licenses one Cloud PC per named user for dedicated, always-on use. Windows 365 Frontline (renamed Windows 365 Flex in 2026, with licensing and features unchanged) licenses a smaller pool of Cloud PCs shared across a larger set of shift-based users, with only a limited number of concurrent connections allowed per license set.
eg: Frontline is the cost-effective pick for shift workers who never overlap, since each Frontline license can serve several named users as long as only one of them is active at a time, so licenses are sized for peak concurrent use rather than headcount.

def: Windows Autopatch is a managed service that takes over update deployment for enrolled devices, automatically organizing them into deployment rings and rolling out Windows quality updates, driver and firmware updates, Microsoft 365 Apps updates, and Edge updates on Microsoft-managed schedules.
prompt: _____ is a managed service that takes over update deployment for enrolled devices, automatically organizing them into deployment rings and rolling out Windows quality updates, driver and firmware updates, Microsoft 365 Apps updates, and Edge updates on Microsoft-managed schedules.
eg: Enrolling a device in Autopatch requires it already be Intune-managed, covered by an eligible Windows license (such as Windows 11 Enterprise E3/E5, which Microsoft 365 E3/E5 include), and meeting prerequisite checks the Autopatch readiness assessment reports on.

def: An update method that applies a subset of security updates to a running Windows instance in memory, without requiring the usual reboot that full monthly cumulative updates need, reducing downtime and restart fatigue for enrolled devices.
eg: Hotpatch releases still land on a baseline cumulative update periodically, since not every fix can be applied in memory, so it reduces reboots rather than eliminating them entirely.

def: Windows devices can be enrolled through Windows Autopilot, Group Policy-based auto-enrollment for already domain-joined devices, a bulk enrollment provisioning package built with Windows Configuration Designer, or manual self-enrollment through Settings for a device already Entra joined or registered.
eg: GPO-based auto-enrollment is specifically for hybrid Entra joined devices that are already domain-joined and simply need to pick up MDM enrollment automatically, rather than a from-scratch provisioning method.

term: Windows Update for Business update rings
def: An Intune policy that controls when and how a group of devices receives quality and feature updates: deferral periods, whether updates install automatically, active hours, and whether the device is part of an early or broad deployment wave.
eg: Rings are commonly staged, with a small pilot ring using a short or zero deferral and progressively larger rings using longer deferrals, so a bad update is caught on a small population before it reaches everyone.

term: Feature update deferral vs quality update deferral
def: A feature update deferral delays a new Windows version, such as moving from one annual release to the next, by up to 365 days. A quality update deferral delays monthly, cumulative security and reliability fixes by up to 30 days. They are configured and deferred independently of each other in the same update ring.
eg: Delaying feature updates does not delay quality updates on the same ring, so a device can still be receiving this month's security patches on a much older feature version.

term: Co-management workloads and the co-management slider
def: A hybrid Entra joined device can be managed by both Configuration Manager and Intune at once. Per-workload sliders, such as Compliance policies, Device Configuration, or Windows Update Policies, individually decide whether Configuration Manager or Intune is authoritative for that specific workload.
eg: Switching a workload's slider to Intune does not uninstall or disable the Configuration Manager client; Configuration Manager still manages every workload whose slider was not moved.

def: A Microsoft-applied block that automatically stops a feature update from being offered to a device that Microsoft has detected has a known compatibility issue, preventing the upgrade until Microsoft resolves the issue and lifts the block, or an administrator deliberately opts the device out of these blocks.
eg: Safeguard holds are Microsoft's own protective mechanism, not something an admin configures directly, though update reporting shows which devices are held and an admin can choose to opt out, which Microsoft advises against until the issue is resolved.

def: A screen that shows provisioning progress during Windows Autopilot and blocks a user from reaching the desktop until required apps and configuration profiles finish installing, so the device is fully ready on first login instead of continuing to configure itself in the background.
eg: ESP settings can be scoped separately for the out-of-box experience and for every subsequent sign-in, which matters for the different Windows Autopilot deployment profile types.

def: Wipes a Windows device back to a business-ready state — reapplying Autopilot provisioning and Intune policies — while keeping the device's Entra ID/Intune enrollment, so it doesn't need to go through Windows Autopilot provisioning from scratch.
eg: This is the fast option for reissuing a device to a new employee or recovering a misconfigured one, since it skips the enrollment step entirely rather than repeating it.

def: A device category is a label an end user can be prompted to choose during enrollment, or that an admin assigns afterward, used mainly for reporting, dynamic group membership, and targeting policy to devices grouped by purpose, such as 'Kiosk' or 'Executive.' A scope tag instead limits which admins can see and manage an object; the two serve different jobs and can both be applied to the same device at once.
eg: Device categories can be surfaced as a required choice during Autopilot or standard enrollment, but changing a device's category after enrollment does not retroactively move it into a dynamic group built on that category until the group's membership is re-evaluated.

term: Group Tag and dynamic device group targeting for Autopilot
def: A free-text attribute set on an Autopilot device registration, often during hardware vendor reservation, that a dynamic Microsoft Entra ID device group can filter on, automatically placing newly registered hardware into the correct group and, through that group's assignment, the correct Autopilot deployment profile with no manual per-device assignment.
eg: Dynamic group membership evaluation is not instantaneous, so a freshly registered device can sit briefly outside its intended group, which is why Microsoft recommends registering hardware and setting its Group Tag well before the device is due to ship.

def: An Intune policy that pins a targeted group of devices to a specific target Windows version, such as holding everyone on 25H2 regardless of what their update ring's feature deferral would otherwise allow, and can stage that rollout gradually. It complements, rather than replaces, an update ring's separate quality-update deferral settings.
eg: A feature update deployment profile can override an update ring's feature deferral in either direction, holding a device back from a newer version or pushing it forward faster, so having both assigned to the same device is a common source of confusion about which version actually lands.

def: A policy that lets Intune manage driver and firmware updates distributed through Windows Update for Business independently of quality and feature updates, letting an admin choose to approve all drivers automatically or review and approve them individually before a targeted group of devices installs them.
eg: Driver updates can be deferred or approved per driver, which matters because a bad OEM driver update, unlike a bad cumulative update, cannot always be resolved by a simple safeguard hold and may need to be blocked at the driver-policy level directly.

def: A deployment type that lets an administrator push an urgent, already-released quality update to a targeted group of devices immediately, bypassing that group's normal update ring deferral and active-hours settings, for scenarios like a zero-day vulnerability that cannot wait for the next scheduled deployment wave.
eg: Expediting is meant for narrow, urgent situations on a limited device count; because it can force an install and restart outside a user's normal active hours, using it broadly defeats the purpose of having deferral rings in the first place.

def: A configuration profile that locks a device into running one app (single-app mode) or a curated small set of apps (multi-app mode), signing in as a designated local or Microsoft Entra ID account with the Start menu, taskbar, and most other Windows UI hidden from the end user. It pairs naturally with a self-deploying Autopilot profile, which needs no user interaction and is commonly used for unattended and shared devices, since this configuration takes over as soon as that unattended provisioning finishes.
eg: Multi-app kiosk mode still enforces AppLocker-style restrictions in the background even though it shows a friendlier, Start-menu-like tile launcher than a rigid single-app kiosk does, so an app that isn't explicitly allow-listed still won't launch even from that friendlier launcher.

def: Delivery Optimization is a Windows peer-to-peer content-sharing technology that lets devices download Windows Update for Business update ring content, Windows Autopatch payloads, and Win32 or Microsoft Store apps from nearby peers on the same network or the internet, instead of pulling every byte individually from Microsoft, reducing WAN bandwidth consumption during large rollouts.

eg: Delivery Optimization is configured through its own settings catalog settings, with modes ranging from HTTP-only (peering disabled) to full internet peering across NAT boundaries; a branch office with limited WAN bandwidth typically restricts peering to the local network group instead of the internet-wide group.

term: Offline domain join (ODJ) for hybrid Autopilot
def: A way to join a device to on-premises AD in which the computer account is created in advance and the join data is delivered as a blob. For hybrid Microsoft Entra join, the Intune Connector for Active Directory creates the computer object and returns that blob, which the Autopilot device applies during the out-of-box experience to complete its domain join.
eg: The ODJ blob does not remove the need for network access: the device still needs line-of-sight to a domain controller during OOBE, which is exactly the problem a split-tunnel VPN that only routes specific corporate traffic can create until a user manually connects first.

def: One Windows 365 feature lets a user sign in to a physical Windows device directly into their Cloud PC at the login screen instead of the local desktop. A second lets a user already signed in locally move back and forth between their local desktop and their Cloud PC from within the same session, similar to switching between virtual desktops.
eg: Boot is about how a session starts, landing straight in the Cloud PC from the lock screen, while Switch is about moving between a local and cloud session once already signed in; a device can support both features at once.

def: Autopilot for existing devices converts a device that is already in service into an Autopilot-managed device by running a Configuration Manager task sequence that reinstalls Windows and applies an Autopilot profile, so it goes through a user-driven Autopilot deployment without the OEM having registered its hardware hash in advance.

eg: This is the path to adopt Autopilot for a fleet of devices already deployed years ago, rather than only for brand-new hardware a reseller or OEM registers at the point of sale.

def: A flow that splits a user-driven Autopilot deployment into two phases. A technician or reseller runs the device phase first, installing device-targeted apps and policies, and the end user later completes only the short user phase. It was formerly called white glove.
eg: At the first setup screen the technician presses the Windows key five times and chooses Provision. It supports user-driven deployments for both Microsoft Entra join and hybrid join, and the user phase shrinks because most of the work already happened.

def: A hardware hash is a device-specific identifier, built from hardware details such as the serial number, that Windows Autopilot uses to recognize a device at first boot. The hash must be registered in the tenant before the device can receive an Autopilot deployment profile.

eg: OEMs and resellers can register hashes for you. Otherwise run the Get-WindowsAutopilotInfo script, which saves a CSV file you import into Intune or uploads the hash directly.

def: A licensing feature that upgrades a licensed Windows Pro device to Windows Enterprise automatically when a user with a Windows Enterprise E3 or E5 license signs in with Microsoft Entra credentials. It needs no product key or reinstall, and the device steps back to Pro when the license lapses.
eg: A typical case is new OEM Pro laptops joined through Autopilot that become Enterprise at the first licensed sign-in. The base Pro edition must already be activated, and Windows Home cannot be stepped up.

def: Group Policy analytics is an Intune tool that imports exported GPO XML files and reports what percentage of each GPO's settings have an MDM equivalent. It also flags deprecated or unsupported settings and can migrate the supported ones into a settings catalog profile.

def: An Administrative templates profile exposes thousands of Windows, Microsoft Edge and Office settings that mirror Group Policy, in a familiar folder tree, and delivers them through Intune. eg: Exam angle: to reproduce an existing GPO setting quickly, choose Administrative templates or the settings catalog. Building a custom OMA-URI profile by hand is the last resort.

def: A device configuration profile type that lets an admin hand-enter settings, each with a URI path, data type and value, to configure a Windows CSP setting that has no built-in Intune interface.
eg: OMA-URI stands for Open Mobile Alliance Uniform Resource Identifier. Custom profiles are error-prone, because a wrong URI or data type simply fails on the device. Check the settings catalog first, since it now covers most CSP settings without hand-typed paths.

def: In a Windows Update for Business update ring, the deadline is the number of days after an update is offered before it installs automatically. The grace period is the extra number of days after the deadline before the device restarts without asking.
eg: Example: a 2-day deadline with a 2-day grace period means install by day 2 and a forced restart by day 4. Setting both to 0 forces the update and restart as soon as possible.

def: Platform scripts are PowerShell scripts for Windows, and shell scripts for macOS, that Intune runs once on assigned devices, in system or user context. Unlike proactive remediations, they have no detection step and no recurring schedule.
prompt: _____ are PowerShell scripts for Windows, and shell scripts for macOS, that Intune runs once on assigned devices, in system or user context. Unlike proactive remediations, they have no detection step and no recurring schedule.
eg: On Windows the Intune Management Extension delivers and runs them. Use a platform script for a one-time task such as setting a registry value, and proactive remediations when the fix must run repeatedly.

def: The primary user is the person Intune records as the main user of a device. User affinity at enrollment decides whether a device is tied to a user, which enables per-user policies and apps, or is userless, as with kiosks and shared devices.
eg: A user-driven Autopilot deployment makes the enrolling user the primary user, while self-deploying mode leaves none. The primary user can be changed later in the device's properties.

term: Apply a device name template in Windows Autopilot
def: An Autopilot deployment profile setting that names each device during enrollment from a pattern: up to 15 characters of letters, numbers, and hyphens (not all numbers), with %SERIAL% for the hardware serial number and %RAND:x% for x random digits. It requires Microsoft Entra join; for hybrid devices only a prefix can be set, in the domain join profile.
eg: A template such as CORP-%RAND:5% gives unique, predictable names without scripts. The name has to fit in 15 characters after the macros expand, so a long prefix plus %SERIAL% can fail on devices with long serial numbers.

term: Choosing Autopilot deployment profiles or device preparation policies
def: Device preparation needs no hardware hash registration, supports Microsoft Entra join only, offers user-driven and automatic modes, and delivers up to 25 essential apps and 10 scripts during OOBE. Classic profiles need device registration but add hybrid join, pre-provisioning, self-deploying, existing-devices modes, user ESP, and up to 100 apps.
eg: Pick device preparation for faster, simpler cloud-native Entra join deployments. Pick classic profiles when the scenario needs hybrid join, a technician pre-provisioning step, a self-deploying kiosk, or more apps than the device preparation limits.

term: Upgrading Windows 10 devices to Windows 11 with Intune
def: Use a feature update deployment profile that targets a Windows 11 version. Devices that meet the requirements upgrade; ineligible devices stay on Windows 10 unless the option to install the latest Windows 10 feature update on devices that cannot run Windows 11 is selected. Endpoint analytics readiness reports show which devices meet hardware requirements.
eg: The checkbox cannot be changed on an existing policy, because changing it ends one deployment and starts two. Create a new policy instead. Submitting the policy accepts the Windows 11 license terms on behalf of users, so no user prompt appears.

term: Windows settings backup and restore (formerly Windows Backup for Organizations)
def: A Windows feature that backs up user settings and the list of Microsoft Store apps for users signed in with Microsoft Entra ID, then restores them on a new device during OOBE or at first sign-in. Backup needs a policy until Windows 11 version 26H2, which turns it on by default for eligible devices, while restore stays off until an admin enables it; backups run about every eight days.
eg: Configure backup with a settings catalog policy. Restore can be turned on tenant-wide for enrollment (Devices > Enrollment > Windows Backup and Restore) or with a settings catalog policy after enrollment. During Autopilot, the profile must be user-driven, not self-deploying.

def: A Cloud PC is built from a gallery image or a custom image. Gallery images are replicated to all regions, updated monthly, and come with or without Microsoft 365 Apps preinstalled. Custom images must be generation 2, generalized, single-session, never joined to a domain, Entra ID, or Intune, and stored as a managed image or in an Azure Compute Gallery.
eg: Images cannot contain FSLogix components or a recovery partition, and multi-session images are not supported. The image is chosen in the provisioning policy.

def: A provisioning policy can place Cloud PCs on a Microsoft-hosted network or on your own virtual network through an Azure network connection (ANC). The ANC is needed for access to on-premises resources and for hybrid Microsoft Entra join, and it needs health checks to pass.
eg: Use the Microsoft-hosted network when Cloud PCs only need internet and cloud apps, since there is nothing to build or maintain. Use an ANC when the Cloud PCs must reach private resources, which brings the extra roles and network requirements.

def: Specialty device management covers devices such as Microsoft Teams Rooms, HoloLens 2, and other AR/VR or smart-screen devices, and needs Intune Plan 2 or the advanced capabilities. Zebra Android devices are tuned with OEMConfig profiles: Zebra OEMConfig Powered by MX for newer Android versions and the legacy OEMConfig app for older ones.
eg: On Zebra devices, do not configure the same top-level group in several OEMConfig profiles, since that creates conflicts, and keep settings in as few profiles as possible because multiple profiles take longer to deploy.

term: Microsoft Tunnel for Mobile Application Management (Tunnel for MAM)
def: An extension of the Microsoft Tunnel VPN gateway to Android and iOS/iPadOS devices that are not enrolled in Intune, so BYOD users reach on-premises resources through managed apps. It requires an existing Tunnel gateway and a license that includes it, such as Intune Plan 2, the Intune Suite or a Microsoft 365 bundle that carries it.
eg: On Android, VPN comes through the Defender app (with Company Portal installed) and can be per-app or device-wide. On iOS/iPadOS it uses the Tunnel for MAM SDK in the app and is per-app only. Edge can enforce strict tunnel mode, which blocks traffic when the VPN is down.

term: Update Microsoft Defender security intelligence remote action
def: A remote action that tells a Windows device to refresh its Microsoft Defender Antivirus definitions immediately; separate quick scan and full scan actions run a scan on demand, all from the device page in Intune.
eg: It is the quick response when a new threat is announced, or when a device missed scheduled updates. It does not change antivirus policy, only triggers an immediate update.

def: Intune can run supported remote actions on up to 100 devices at once from Devices > All devices > Bulk device actions, for example wipe, retire, and delete. Bulk requests count toward the tenant's daily limit for each action, together with individual and Graph API requests.

eg: It suits end-of-term resets or fleet-wide restarts. For larger sets, split the work into several batches or use the Microsoft Graph API, remembering that the daily limit is shared across all submission methods.

def: A remote action that generates a new recovery key for the OS drive of an encrypted Windows device, so a key that was read aloud or exposed becomes useless. Run it from the device page under Secure; roles such as Help Desk Operator and Endpoint Security Manager include the permission.
eg: The old key stops working once the new one is escrowed. Check that the new key has been escrowed to Microsoft Entra ID before relying on it.

def: The action forces a new password for the managed local administrator account outside the Windows LAPS schedule, for example after a suspected compromise or a support session. It works on corporate-owned Windows devices that are Entra joined or hybrid joined and already back up their LAPS password to Microsoft Entra ID.
eg: It also works for macOS devices enrolled with Automated Device Enrollment whose local admin account is defined in the ADE profile. A custom role needs the Rotate Local Admin Password remote task permission.

def: Enrollment time grouping lets an Intune enrollment policy place a device in a static Microsoft Entra security group during enrollment, so group-targeted policies and apps reach the device earlier in setup. It works with Apple automated device enrollment (iOS/iPadOS and macOS), Android Enterprise corporate-owned enrollment and Windows Autopilot device preparation.
prompt: _____ lets an Intune enrollment policy place a device in a static Microsoft Entra security group during enrollment, so group-targeted policies and apps reach the device earlier in setup. It works with Apple automated device enrollment (iOS/iPadOS and macOS), Android Enterprise corporate-owned enrollment and Windows Autopilot device preparation.
eg: Normally a device only lands in a dynamic group after enrollment finishes, so required apps and policies arrive late. Targeting a static group at enrollment time avoids that delay. Assignment filters are the complementary tool for narrowing a profile to the right devices.

term: Software update policies for iOS/iPadOS and macOS
def: Apple update policies are created in the settings catalog with Declarative Device Management. A Latest version policy installs the newest eligible OS after a delay in days at an install time, while a Targeted version policy requires a specific OS version by a deadline and can show a details URL. The older MDM-based update policies are deprecated.
eg: Devices enforce the declaration on their own, so the device does not wait for an MDM command. Use targeted version when an app must be validated first, and latest version for fast patching with minimal IT effort.

def: A capability that lets Intune manage firmware updates for corporate-owned Android Enterprise devices (fully managed, dedicated, and corporate-owned work profile) through the device maker's own update service, currently Samsung's and Zebra's. Where that service is unavailable, a device restrictions profile controls system updates and can set a freeze period.
eg: FOTA is an Intune advanced capability (Plan 2, the Suite or a Microsoft 365 bundle that includes it). Samsung devices use Knox E-FOTA and Zebra devices use LifeGuard OTA. A freeze period blocks over-the-air updates for a defined window, such as a holiday sales peak, but not every manufacturer supports over-the-air control.

def: Deployment plans (public preview) are reusable templates that define rings of group assignments with deferral days and hours between them. A deployment applies a plan to a specific app or policy so it reaches devices in controlled stages, found under Devices > Manage devices > Deployments.
prompt: _____ (public preview) are reusable templates that define rings of group assignments with deferral days and hours between them. A deployment applies a plan to a specific app or policy so it reaches devices in controlled stages, found under Devices > Manage devices > Deployments.
eg: A ring that uses the All users or All devices virtual group is always the last ring. Plans hold no payload; the payload is chosen when you create the deployment.

def: The setting that determines which management service is in charge of a tenant's mobile device management. New Intune tenants are set to Intune automatically, so this is mostly a legacy concern: older tenants may still have had the authority set to Configuration Manager hybrid MDM or Office 365 MDM before moving to Intune, and co-management is now the standard hybrid approach.
eg: Enrollment cannot work without a valid MDM authority, but because it is set automatically on new tenants, a tenant-wide enrollment failure is more likely caused by the MDM user scope, an enrollment restriction, or an expired APNs certificate than by the authority itself.

term: Enrollment restrictions: platform vs device limit
def: A device platform restriction blocks or allows enrollment by OS type, such as Windows, iOS/iPadOS, Android, or macOS, and can require a minimum or maximum OS version. A device limit restriction caps how many devices a single user is allowed to enroll, independent of platform.
eg: Restrictions of the same type are ranked by priority, and a user gets only the highest-priority restriction assigned to one of their groups (they are not merged), with a built-in default restriction applying to anyone no assigned restriction covers.

term: Device configuration profiles vs the settings catalog
def: Older, template-based device configuration profiles group related settings into purpose-built templates, such as Endpoint Protection or Device restrictions. The settings catalog instead exposes essentially every available CSP-backed setting individually, searchable and combinable into one custom profile.
eg: Microsoft has been steering new profile creation toward the settings catalog because it always reflects the latest available settings, while some older templates are no longer being updated with new options.

term: Microsoft Entra device states: joined, hybrid joined, and registered
def: A Microsoft Entra joined device is owned by the organization and knows only Entra ID, with no on-premises AD account. A hybrid Entra joined device is joined to on-premises AD and also registered with Entra ID. A Microsoft Entra registered device is typically a personal or BYOD device that has only added an Entra ID account without full organizational join.
eg: Joined and hybrid joined devices are organization-owned and receive the full range of Intune device-level compliance and configuration control; a registered BYOD device is usually protected through lighter-touch mobile application management instead.

def: Intune device management is included in Microsoft 365 E3/E5, Enterprise Mobility + Security (EMS) E3/E5, or as a standalone Intune Plan license. Windows 365 Cloud PC requires its own separate per-user Cloud PC license, Enterprise or Frontline (now called Flex), layered on top of whatever license already provides the user's Intune management.
eg: A user without an Intune-capable license can still technically be assigned policy, but their devices will not actually enroll or receive it; licensing gates enrollment itself, not just policy delivery.

def: A label that limits which Intune administrators can see and manage a given policy, app, or device, letting role-based delegation, such as a regional helpdesk team, apply only to the objects marked for their team, instead of the entire tenant's configuration.
eg: Scope tags control visibility and management rights for admins; they do not change which end users or devices a policy is assigned to and applies against.

term: The Intune Connector for Active Directory
def: The Intune Connector for Active Directory is an on-premises agent that lets Autopilot hybrid Entra join create the computer object in on-premises AD during provisioning, bridging cloud-based Autopilot provisioning with an on-premises domain join step.

eg: Without this connector installed and healthy, a hybrid Entra join Autopilot profile fails at the domain-join stage even though every other Autopilot configuration is correct.

term: Configuration profile assignment conflicts and filters
def: When two assigned configuration profiles set the same setting differently for the same device, Intune reports a conflict and neither value is applied for that setting until the conflict is resolved. Assignment filters narrow which devices in an assigned group actually receive a profile, app, or policy, based on device properties like OS version or manufacturer.
eg: A filter is applied on top of a group assignment, not instead of it; a device must both be in the assigned group and match the filter to receive the item.

def: A VPN gateway solution managed through Intune that runs in a container on a Linux server and gives managed iOS/iPadOS and Android Enterprise devices per-app or device-wide access to on-premises resources, with Microsoft Entra authentication and Conditional Access. Devices use the Microsoft Defender app as the VPN client together with an Intune VPN profile.
eg: Tunnel for MAM, an Intune Plan 2 capability, extends the same gateway to Android and iOS devices that are not enrolled in Intune, so a BYOD app can use the tunnel without full device management.

def: Tenant attach uploads Configuration Manager device and collection data into the Intune admin center so an admin can see ConfigMgr-managed devices and run a limited set of remote actions, like an app install or a device sync, directly from the cloud console, without moving any co-management workload to Intune or fully enrolling the device.
prompt: _____ uploads Configuration Manager device and collection data into the Intune admin center so an admin can see ConfigMgr-managed devices and run a limited set of remote actions, like an app install or a device sync, directly from the cloud console, without moving any co-management workload to Intune or fully enrolling the device.
eg: Tenant attach is purely a visibility and remote-action bridge; it does not make Intune policy-authoritative for anything, which is the key distinction from actually shifting a co-management workload slider to Intune.

term: Azure Virtual Desktop vs Windows 365 vs physical endpoints
def: Azure Virtual Desktop hosts multi-session or personal virtual desktops on infrastructure the organization configures and scales itself in Azure, billed for consumed compute. Windows 365 is a fixed-price, per-user Cloud PC with dedicated, always-on infrastructure Microsoft manages behind the scenes. Both differ from a physical endpoint, a locally running device that is enrolled and managed through Intune the same way regardless of which management tasks apply.
eg: A Cloud PC and a physical endpoint both show up as ordinary managed devices in Intune and can receive the same compliance policies and configuration profiles, so a scenario testing which management approach applies often hinges on licensing and infrastructure model, not on what Intune itself can configure.

term: Dynamic vs assigned (static) Microsoft Entra ID groups for Intune targeting
def: An assigned group requires an admin to manually add or remove each member, giving exact, deliberate control. A dynamic group instead evaluates a membership rule, such as device OS, model, or a Group Tag, and automatically adds or removes members as their attributes change, which is what lets new Autopilot hardware or a re-tagged device land in the right policy target with no manual step.
eg: Dynamic group membership evaluation can lag by minutes, so a policy that must apply the instant a device is provisioned, such as during the Enrollment Status Page, is safer targeted through an assigned group or a Group Tag set before shipping rather than a rule evaluated after the fact.

term: macOS and Android Enterprise device management in Intune
def: Intune manages non-Windows platforms through their own native enrollment mechanisms layered under the same policy engine used for Windows: macOS enrolls through Apple's Automated Device Enrollment or user-initiated Company Portal app enrollment, while Android Enterprise offers a fully managed corporate-owned mode or a work profile mode that keeps a separate, IT-managed container alongside personal apps on a personal device. Platform enrollment restrictions still govern which of these platforms is even allowed to enroll in the first place.
eg: Android Enterprise's work profile mode is the closest Android analogue to an app protection policy on an unenrolled device — both keep corporate data in an isolated, wipeable container without touching everything else on a personal device, though a work profile does still require MDM enrollment while an app protection policy does not.

def: A device's ownership property, corporate or personal, set at enrollment, shapes what the Company Portal app shows the user and which remote action Intune permits an admin to take on it. On a corporate-owned device, Wipe is available to reset the device entirely back to factory settings for reissue or decommission, while on a personal MDM-enrolled device, Retire is the action that actually respects the organization's rights, removing only corporate data, apps, and management.
eg: Ownership is usually set automatically by the enrollment method used, such as Autopilot for corporate-owned or self-service Company Portal enrollment for personal, but it can also be corrected manually in the Intune console if a device was enrolled through the wrong path and shows the wrong ownership type.

def: The Apple-issued certificate that a tenant uploads to Intune to establish trust with Apple's push notification service is a hard prerequisite for managing any iOS/iPadOS or macOS device, including Automated Device Enrollment — without a valid, unexpired one, Intune cannot push MDM commands to Apple devices at all.
eg: An APNs certificate must be renewed annually with the same Apple ID that originally created it; letting it expire doesn't just block new enrollments, it also stops Intune managing every already-enrolled Apple device in the tenant until the certificate is renewed (Apple allows a 30-day grace period to renew after expiry).

def: A Microsoft Entra ID container that scopes a delegated admin's role, such as User Administrator, to only the users, groups, or devices placed inside it, letting a regional team manage its own directory objects without seeing or touching the rest of the tenant.
eg: An administrative unit delegates directory-level administration in Entra ID itself; it is a different layer from scope tags, which instead limit what an Intune role can see and manage among Intune objects like policies, apps, and devices.

def: Two kinds of connection profile, each deployed as its own device configuration or settings catalog profile type, push connection settings, such as server address, authentication method, and SSID, to managed devices automatically, and commonly pair with a certificate profile sourced from Microsoft Cloud PKI or SCEP so the device authenticates with a certificate instead of a typed password.
eg: Deploying the certificate profile and the VPN or Wi-Fi profile to the same device group is what actually lets authentication succeed silently; the connection profile alone, with no matching certificate delivered to the device, fails at the authentication step.

term: Corporate device identifiers (IMEI/serial number allow list)
def: A corporate device identifiers list lets an admin upload a set of IMEI numbers or serial numbers to mark specific hardware as corporate-owned at enrollment, separate from the platform and device-limit enrollment restrictions, which instead cap enrollment by OS type or by how many devices one user can add.
prompt: A _____ list lets an admin upload a set of IMEI numbers or serial numbers to mark specific hardware as corporate-owned at enrollment, separate from the platform and device-limit enrollment restrictions, which instead cap enrollment by OS type or by how many devices one user can add.
eg: Marking a device as corporate-owned through its identifier matters because device ownership controls which Company Portal experience and which remote actions, such as Wipe or Retire, an admin is allowed to use against it later.

def: A SCEP certificate profile has each device generate its own key pair and request a certificate from a certification authority using the Simple Certificate Enrollment Protocol. Because the private key never leaves the device, it suits Wi-Fi, VPN and email authentication certificates.
prompt: A _____ has each device generate its own key pair and request a certificate from a certification authority using the Simple Certificate Enrollment Protocol. Because the private key never leaves the device, it suits Wi-Fi, VPN and email authentication certificates.
eg: It needs a trusted certificate profile deployed first, so the device trusts the CA chain. With an on-premises CA the requests go through NDES, while Cloud PKI can issue SCEP certificates without it.

term: PKCS certificate profile and imported PFX certificates
def: One type of certificate profile has the Intune Certificate Connector request a certificate from an on-premises CA on the device's behalf, so the key pair is not created by the device. A companion option lets you upload existing user certificates with their private keys, for example for S/MIME email, for Intune to deliver.
eg: Choose PKCS when the CA team will not expose NDES. Choose imported PFX only when existing private keys must be preserved, such as S/MIME certificates users need to read old mail.

def: NDES is the Windows Server role that implements SCEP for Active Directory Certificate Services. For Intune SCEP profiles it sits between devices and the on-premises CA, and the Intune Certificate Connector installed on the NDES server relays validation with Intune.
prompt: _____ is the Windows Server role that implements SCEP for Active Directory Certificate Services. For Intune SCEP profiles it sits between devices and the on-premises CA, and the Intune Certificate Connector installed on the _____ server relays validation with Intune.
eg: Scenarios that forbid an on-premises CA or NDES server point to Microsoft Cloud PKI, which removes both the NDES server and the connector.

def: A trusted certificate profile deploys a root or intermediate CA certificate, supplied as a .cer file, to devices so they trust certificates issued by that CA. SCEP, PKCS, Wi-Fi and VPN profiles that rely on the CA depend on it reaching the device first.
prompt: A _____ deploys a root or intermediate CA certificate, supplied as a .cer file, to devices so they trust certificates issued by that CA. SCEP, PKCS, Wi-Fi and VPN profiles that rely on the CA depend on it reaching the device first.
eg: A classic fault: the Wi-Fi profile references a trusted certificate profile that was never assigned to the device group, so server validation fails. Assign trusted, certificate and Wi-Fi profiles to the same group.

def: Apple's bulk enrollment program, formerly the Device Enrollment Program, that lets an organization buy Apple devices through Apple Business Manager or Apple School Manager and have them enroll in Intune automatically at first setup. Devices can be enrolled as supervised.
eg: Setup: create an ADE token in Apple Business Manager, upload it to Intune, then assign an enrollment profile to the devices. It also requires a valid APNs certificate.

term: Android zero-touch enrollment and Samsung Knox Mobile Enrollment
def: Both are bulk enrollment methods for corporate-owned Android Enterprise devices that start enrollment straight out of the box. One is Google's reseller-managed portal, and the other is Samsung's equivalent for Knox devices.
eg: Alternatives are a QR code, NFC or a typed token. Pick zero-touch or Knox when hundreds of new phones ship to users and nobody in IT handles them first.

def: A higher level of management on corporate-owned iPhones and iPads that unlocks controls unavailable on personal devices, such as Lost Mode and single-app kiosk mode. Devices reach it through Automated Device Enrollment or Apple Configurator.
eg: If a feature is supervised-only, personal devices enrolled through Company Portal cannot use it. Only devices that came in through ADE or Apple Configurator qualify.

def: A setting that enrolls Windows devices in Intune when a user signs in with Microsoft Entra credentials and falls inside the user scope set in Entra ID Mobility (MDM and MAM). That scope can be set to None, Some (selected groups) or All.
eg: If devices join Entra ID but never appear in Intune, check the MDM user scope first. Hybrid joined devices also need the automatic enrollment Group Policy or Configuration Manager setting.

def: Intune RBAC gives admins only the permissions they need, through built-in roles such as Help Desk Operator, Policy and Profile Manager, Application Manager and Endpoint Security Manager, or through custom roles. A role assignment links admin groups to the scope groups and scope tags they may manage.
prompt: Intune _____ gives admins only the permissions they need, through built-in roles such as Help Desk Operator, Policy and Profile Manager, Application Manager and Endpoint Security Manager, or through custom roles. A role assignment links admin groups to the scope groups and scope tags they may manage.
eg: Example: give the regional help desk Help Desk Operator, limited by a scope tag to one region, so they can run remote actions only on those devices.

term: Android Enterprise enrollment options in Intune
def: Personally owned devices use a work profile (BYOD). Corporate-owned options are fully managed (COBO, whole device managed for one user), dedicated (COSU, user-less kiosk or shared devices) and corporate-owned work profile (COPE, a work profile on a company device). Android Open Source Project and device administrator are further, narrower options.
eg: Pick by ownership and whether a user is attached: shared kiosks need dedicated, company phones that mix work and personal use fit COPE, and personal phones get a work profile. After an enrollment profile is assigned, do not rename it, because that can break future enrollments; create a new profile instead.

def: Start with the enrollment failures report under Devices > Monitor, then check the usual causes: a platform or device-limit restriction that blocks the device, a user without an Intune license, the MDM user scope not covering the user, a missing Apple or Google connection, or a wrong enrollment profile assignment.
eg: The failure reason in the report usually points at the setting to change. Fix it at the source, such as a restriction priority or a license, then have the user retry; retrying without a fix repeats the failure.

def: Cloud PCs are managed with Intune role-based access control plus Windows 365 roles: the Windows 365 Administrator Microsoft Entra role manages Cloud PCs broadly, while in Intune the Cloud PC Administrator role manages images, network connections and provisioning, and Cloud PC Reader gives read-only access to the Windows 365 node.
eg: When an Azure network connection is used, Windows 365 needs the Windows 365 Network Interface Contributor role on the connection's resource group and the Windows 365 Network User role on its virtual network. These are given to the Windows 365 service, not to admins.

term: Zero Trust security recommendations for Intune
def: Microsoft publishes security recommendations for configuring Intune, and a Zero Trust Assessment can test them automatically. Examples are enforcing scope tags, enrollment notifications, automatic Windows enrollment, and compliance policies for every platform, so unmanaged or unevaluated endpoints cannot get through.
eg: Zero Trust for endpoints means verify explicitly, use least privilege, and assume breach: require compliant devices in Conditional Access, give admins only the roles and scope they need, and use endpoint security policies so a compromised device is contained.

term: Compliance policy settings and actions for noncompliance
def: A compliance policy defines requirements a device must meet, such as minimum OS version, encryption, or a passcode. Actions for noncompliance define what happens when a device fails, each on its own schedule: send an email to the user, mark the device noncompliant, retire it, and so on. The schedule on the Mark device noncompliant action is the grace period, and once it elapses the device is noncompliant and Conditional Access can block access.
eg: During the grace period the device shows as In grace period and Conditional Access still treats it as compliant, so the schedule delays the noncompliant status, and therefore the access block, rather than being a separate step after it.

term: Conditional Access grant control: require device to be marked compliant
def: This Conditional Access grant control checks the device's compliance status recorded by Intune at sign-in time, blocking access unless that specific device, not just any device belonging to the user, is currently compliant.
eg: This grant control is device-bound, not user-bound; a compliant device satisfies it even for a risky sign-in location, while the same user on a noncompliant personal device is blocked even from a trusted network.

term: Onboarding devices to Microsoft Defender for Endpoint via Intune
def: A two-step setup: an admin first enables the tenant-level connection between Intune and Defender for Endpoint, after which Intune can push an onboarding configuration profile to enrolled devices, connecting them to the Defender for Endpoint service without a per-device script so their risk signals flow back into Intune.
eg: The connection is switched on once under Tenant administration > Connectors and tokens > Microsoft Defender for Endpoint. Until it is on, an onboarding policy has nothing to connect to, so the connector is the first thing to check when devices never appear in the Defender portal.

def: A Microsoft-curated group of preconfigured settings, based on Microsoft-recommended and industry-standard values, that can be assigned as a starting point and then customized, instead of building an equivalent settings catalog profile completely from scratch.
eg: Baselines are versioned; a newer baseline version can introduce new or changed default settings, and an admin must explicitly move a profile instance to the new version to actually pick up those changes.

term: BitLocker and disk encryption policy via Intune
def: An endpoint security disk encryption or settings catalog profile can require Windows' built-in full-volume encryption on a device, control recovery key storage in Microsoft Entra ID, silently enable encryption without prompting the user, and specify the encryption method and cipher strength.
eg: Storing the recovery key in Microsoft Entra ID lets a help desk technician look it up during a self-service or assisted recovery, without the end user ever having written it down themselves.

def: Endpoint Privilege Management lets a standard, non-administrator user elevate specific, approved applications to run with administrator rights, without granting that user full local administrator rights on the device at all.
prompt: _____ lets a standard, non-administrator user elevate specific, approved applications to run with administrator rights, without granting that user full local administrator rights on the device at all.
eg: EPM elevation rules can be automatic, user-confirmed (optionally requiring a business justification, authentication, or both), or support-approved, where the request waits for an IT admin to approve it in the Intune admin center before the elevation is granted for that one application.

def: Attack surface reduction rules, delivered through Intune endpoint security policy, target specific, commonly exploited behaviors, such as Office apps creating child processes or credential theft from LSASS, and can block, audit, or warn on them independent of full antivirus signature detection.
prompt: _____, delivered through Intune endpoint security policy, target specific, commonly exploited behaviors, such as Office apps creating child processes or credential theft from LSASS, and can block, audit, or warn on them independent of full antivirus signature detection.
eg: Deploying ASR rules in audit mode first, and reviewing the resulting events, is the recommended way to find false positives before actually enforcing block mode against a production population.

def: Windows Hello for Business replaces password sign-in with a PIN or biometric, face or fingerprint, that unlocks a cryptographic key pair or certificate stored on the device (in its TPM where available), providing phishing-resistant authentication that never transmits a shared secret over the network, and it is deployed and configured through an Intune device configuration or settings catalog profile.
prompt: _____ replaces password sign-in with a PIN or biometric, face or fingerprint, that unlocks a cryptographic key pair or certificate stored on the device (in its TPM where available), providing phishing-resistant authentication that never transmits a shared secret over the network, and it is deployed and configured through an Intune device configuration or settings catalog profile.
eg: Because the credential is bound to the specific device's TPM, a Windows Hello for Business PIN set up on one machine cannot be used to sign in on another; a user must enroll it separately on each device they use.

def: An Intune endpoint security firewall policy configures the built-in Microsoft Defender Firewall's profiles, domain, private, and public, including default inbound/outbound actions and specific port or app rules, letting an admin enforce consistent network-level blocking without relying on a third-party firewall management tool.
prompt: An Intune _____ configures the built-in Microsoft Defender Firewall's profiles, domain, private, and public, including default inbound/outbound actions and specific port or app rules, letting an admin enforce consistent network-level blocking without relying on a third-party firewall management tool.
eg: Firewall policy settings are evaluated per network profile, so a laptop can correctly enforce a strict public-profile rule set at a coffee shop while applying a more permissive rule set on the trusted corporate network, without any separate policy switch.

def: Windows LAPS, configured through an Intune endpoint security or settings catalog policy, automatically randomizes and periodically rotates a device's local administrator account password and backs the current password up to Microsoft Entra ID or on-premises AD, so a help desk admin can retrieve it when needed instead of every device sharing one static local admin credential.
prompt: Windows _____, configured through an Intune endpoint security or settings catalog policy, automatically randomizes and periodically rotates a device's local administrator account password and backs the current password up to Microsoft Entra ID or on-premises AD, so a help desk admin can retrieve it when needed instead of every device sharing one static local admin credential.
eg: Because each device gets its own randomized password, compromising the local admin credential on one machine no longer gives an attacker a password that also works on every other device in the fleet, closing off a classic lateral-movement path.

term: Conditional Access policies and Intune-aware grant controls
def: A Conditional Access policy pairs a set of conditions, such as user, app, location, or device platform, with a grant control that decides what is required before access is allowed. Two grant controls specifically read Intune signals: require device to be marked as compliant checks the signing-in device's own compliance status, while require app protection policy checks that the client app is one that supports app protection and that a compliant app protection policy is actually applied to it (the older require approved client app control was retired in June 2026).
eg: A single Conditional Access policy can combine several grant controls with either a 'require all selected controls' or 'require one of the selected controls' setting, which is what lets one policy accommodate both a fully enrolled corporate laptop and an unenrolled personal phone running an approved, protected app.

def: An Intune endpoint security policy that configures the built-in Windows malware scanner's settings, such as cloud-delivered protection level, real-time protection, scheduled and quick scan behavior, and scan exclusions, independent of the separate attack surface reduction rules and firewall policy nodes in endpoint security.
eg: Raising cloud-delivered protection to its highest blocking level trades a small amount of scan latency, while a file is checked against the cloud, for faster coverage of brand-new malware that a signature-only, offline-only configuration would miss.

term: Account protection policy (local user group membership)
def: An Intune endpoint security Account protection policy can enforce which users or groups belong to a device's local groups, such as the local Administrators group, continuously reapplying the defined membership so anyone added outside of policy is automatically removed the next time the policy evaluates.
prompt: An Intune endpoint security _____ can enforce which users or groups belong to a device's local groups, such as the local Administrators group, continuously reapplying the defined membership so anyone added outside of policy is automatically removed the next time the policy evaluates.
eg: This is a different control from Windows LAPS: Account protection decides who is allowed to be a local administrator at all, while LAPS instead randomizes and rotates the password of whichever local administrator account already exists.

def: An iOS/iPadOS or Android compliance policy setting that automatically fails compliance for any device Intune detects has had its OS-level restrictions bypassed, since such a device can no longer be trusted to enforce the rest of the policy's own settings.
eg: This setting pairs naturally with a compliance policy's actions for noncompliance: a device that fails jailbreak detection can trigger the same scheduled actions, up to losing Conditional Access-gated access, as any other failed compliance rule.

def: Tamper protection, enabled through an Intune endpoint security Antivirus policy or security baseline, locks core Microsoft Defender Antivirus settings, such as real-time protection and cloud-delivered protection, against being changed locally, including by a signed-in local administrator, so a compromised or careless admin session cannot quietly disable antivirus protection on the device.
prompt: _____, enabled through an Intune endpoint security Antivirus policy or security baseline, locks core Microsoft Defender Antivirus settings, such as real-time protection and cloud-delivered protection, against being changed locally, including by a signed-in local administrator, so a compromised or careless admin session cannot quietly disable antivirus protection on the device.
eg: Because tamper protection blocks changes made directly on the device itself, an admin who genuinely needs to adjust a protected setting must do so centrally through the Intune policy, not by editing the setting locally on the endpoint.

def: A custom entry, managed in the Microsoft Defender portal and scoped to onboarded devices, that lets an admin explicitly allow or block a specific file, certificate, IP address, or URL/domain by its exact identifier, overriding Defender's normal detection logic for just that one item across every onboarded device.
eg: Indicators are useful for two opposite situations at once: blocking a specific malicious hash security research has identified, or allowing a legitimate internal tool that antivirus heuristics keep misidentifying as suspicious.

term: BitLocker encryption type: used space only vs full disk
def: An Intune encryption profile's BitLocker settings let an admin choose used space only encryption, which encrypts only the sectors currently holding data and finishes faster, or full disk encryption, which also encrypts every empty sector and takes longer but leaves no unencrypted free space that could later retain recoverable traces of deleted data.
eg: Used space only is the common default for a brand-new device with no prior unencrypted data ever written to it, while full disk encryption is the safer choice for a drive that was previously used unencrypted before BitLocker was turned on.

term: Device control policy for removable storage
def: An Intune endpoint security policy, part of the attack surface reduction category, can block or restrict removable storage such as USB drives, by device class or by specific hardware ID, preventing data exfiltration or malware introduction through removable media without having to physically disable USB ports.
eg: Device control can be scoped narrowly, such as allowing only specific, approved USB device IDs while blocking every other removable drive, rather than an all-or-nothing block on every USB port.

def: Credential Guard uses virtualization-based security to isolate and protect cached domain credentials and NTLM hashes in a secured enclave the operating system itself cannot access, so even malware running with local administrator rights cannot extract reusable credentials from an infected device.
prompt: _____ uses virtualization-based security to isolate and protect cached domain credentials and NTLM hashes in a secured enclave the operating system itself cannot access, so even malware running with local administrator rights cannot extract reusable credentials from an infected device.
eg: Credential Guard addresses the same credential-theft-from-LSASS problem that attack surface reduction (ASR) rules can also target, but through hardware-backed isolation instead of behavior-based blocking.

def: Network protection is a Microsoft Defender feature that stops apps and processes on a device from connecting to low-reputation or malicious IP addresses and domains. It can run in block or audit mode, and custom URL and domain indicators from Defender for Endpoint depend on it.
prompt: _____ is a Microsoft Defender feature that stops apps and processes on a device from connecting to low-reputation or malicious IP addresses and domains. It can run in block or audit mode, and custom URL and domain indicators from Defender for Endpoint depend on it.
eg: Start in audit mode to see which destinations would be blocked, then switch to block. Enable it with an Intune endpoint security policy or a settings catalog profile.

def: Controlled folder access protects designated folders, such as Documents and Pictures, from changes by untrusted apps, which helps stop ransomware from encrypting files. Admins can add protected folders and allow specific apps.
prompt: _____ protects designated folders, such as Documents and Pictures, from changes by untrusted apps, which helps stop ransomware from encrypting files. Admins can add protected folders and allow specific apps.
eg: Run it in audit mode first, because line-of-business apps that write to Documents can be blocked until they are allowed. It guards folders, unlike network protection, which guards connections.

def: Exploit protection applies memory-corruption mitigations, such as control flow guard and address space layout randomization, to the whole system or to specific apps. Settings are saved as an XML file and deployed with an Intune endpoint security policy.
prompt: _____ applies memory-corruption mitigations, such as control flow guard and address space layout randomization, to the whole system or to specific apps. Settings are saved as an XML file and deployed with an Intune endpoint security policy.
eg: Build the XML on a reference PC from the Windows Security exploit protection settings, export it, and upload it to the Intune exploit protection policy. It replaces the older EMET tool.

def: A reputation-based protection that checks websites, downloads and apps against a Microsoft reputation service and warns or blocks users from phishing sites, malware sites and unrecognized files. Intune can enforce it and stop users from bypassing the warnings.
eg: A policy setting can remove the option to click through a warning. SmartScreen reputation data also feeds network protection, which extends the same blocking to traffic from other apps.

def: PUA protection in Microsoft Defender Antivirus blocks or audits software that is not strictly malware but is unwanted, such as adware, bundled installers and cryptominers. It is configured as enabled, audit mode or disabled.
prompt: _____ protection in Microsoft Defender Antivirus blocks or audits software that is not strictly malware but is unwanted, such as adware, bundled installers and cryptominers. It is configured as enabled, audit mode or disabled.
eg: The Intune Microsoft Defender Antivirus policy has a Potentially unwanted application setting. Audit mode logs detections without blocking, which shows what would be hit before enforcing.

def: A Mobile Threat Defense connector lets a partner app on iOS/iPadOS or Android, such as Microsoft Defender for Endpoint on mobile, report a device's threat level to Intune. A compliance policy can then mark devices above an allowed risk level as noncompliant, so Conditional Access can block them.
prompt: A _____ lets a partner app on iOS/iPadOS or Android, such as Microsoft Defender for Endpoint on mobile, report a device's threat level to Intune. A compliance policy can then mark devices above an allowed risk level as noncompliant, so Conditional Access can block them.
eg: Setup: enable the MTD connector, deploy the MTD app, add the machine risk score requirement to a compliance policy, and require compliant devices in Conditional Access.

term: Windows device health attestation: Secure Boot, BitLocker and code integrity
def: Intune Windows compliance policies can require that a device booted into a trusted state. A health attestation service checks BitLocker, Secure Boot and code integrity using measurements the Trusted Platform Module recorded at boot, and a failed check marks the device noncompliant.
eg: Windows 10 uses the Device Health Attestation service, while Windows 11 in the commercial cloud uses Microsoft Azure Attestation. A device whose TPM is missing or not ready can fail these checks.

term: Compliance policy settings: no-policy default and validity period
def: Tenant-wide compliance policy settings decide how Intune treats a device with no assigned compliance policy, as Compliant by default or as Not compliant. They also set how many days, 1 to 120 with a default of 30, a device may go without reporting before it is treated as noncompliant.
eg: Set Mark devices with no compliance policy assigned as to Not compliant when Conditional Access requires compliance. Otherwise an unassigned device slips through as compliant.

def: The built-in full-disk encryption on macOS. An Intune endpoint security disk encryption policy can turn it on and escrow the personal recovery key in Intune, so the key can be recovered later, including by the user from Company Portal.
eg: It is the macOS counterpart to BitLocker policy. A compliance policy can require encryption, and a Rotate FileVault recovery key remote action issues a replacement key.

def: A policy type in Intune endpoint security deploys the Microsoft Defender for Endpoint onboarding configuration, plus settings such as sample sharing and telemetry reporting frequency, to devices through a policy assigned to device groups. The Defender for Endpoint connector must be turned on first.
eg: Onboarding makes the device visible in the Microsoft Defender portal, where analysts investigate alerts, triage incidents, and can isolate or scan a device. Intune then uses the device risk level in compliance policies and Conditional Access.

def: The numbered releases of an Intune security baseline (Windows, Edge, Microsoft 365 Apps, Windows 365). Each Windows release gets a new one, such as Windows 11 version 26H2, and existing profiles never update automatically, so an admin must create a new profile or update one to the new release.
eg: Review the changed settings before moving to a newer version, since defaults can change and some settings are retired. Use a pilot group first, then widen the assignment.

term: Defender for Endpoint integration with Intune compliance
def: Once Intune is connected to Microsoft Defender for Endpoint and Windows devices are onboarded, a compliance policy can require a machine risk score at or below a chosen level. A device above that level is marked noncompliant, and Conditional Access can then block it from company resources until it is remediated.
eg: The risk level comes from Defender for Endpoint's detection of active threats, not from Intune settings. Pair it with actions for noncompliance so the user is notified or the device is retired after a grace period.

term: Intune app deployment intents: required, available, and uninstall
def: A required assignment installs an app automatically on every targeted device or user with no action needed. An available assignment lists the app in the Company Portal so a user can choose to install it. An uninstall assignment removes the app from targeted devices or users.
eg: An app can carry different intents for different assigned groups simultaneously; required for one department's group while merely available for everyone else.

term: App protection policies (MAM) vs mobile device management
def: Policies that apply data-protection controls, like requiring a PIN, blocking copy/paste to unmanaged apps, and remote wipe of just that app's corporate data, at the application level rather than managing the whole device the way mobile device management does. That app-level scope is exactly why they are central to BYOD scenarios.
eg: Because app protection policy enforcement does not require device enrollment, it is the standard answer whenever a scenario needs to protect corporate data on a personal device the organization does not otherwise manage.

def: A policy that pushes predefined settings into a managed app, such as a default server URL or a disabled feature flag, at install or launch time, removing the need for a user to manually configure the app themselves after installation.
eg: App configuration policies can target either managed devices (MDM-based) or managed apps regardless of enrollment (MAM-based), matching whichever app protection model the target population uses.

term: Conditional Access grant control: require approved client app / app protection policy
def: The older require approved client app grant control only checked that sign-in came from a Microsoft-approved app, like Outlook or Teams, and Microsoft retired it in June 2026 in favor of require app protection policy. That current grant control goes further, requiring that a compliant app protection policy is actually applied to the app.
eg: Require app protection policy is what lets an organization allow mail access from a personal, unenrolled phone while still blocking a generic, unmanaged mail client from connecting to the same mailbox; policies that still reference the retired approved-client-app control should be migrated to it.

term: Microsoft Cloud PKI for Microsoft Intune
def: A cloud-hosted certificate authority service built into Intune that issues and manages certificates for device and user authentication, such as Wi-Fi, VPN, or app authentication, without standing up and maintaining an on-premises certificate authority or NDES infrastructure.
eg: Cloud PKI eliminates the need for the on-premises Network Device Enrollment Service (NDES) and its connector that a traditional Intune certificate connector deployment previously required.

def: Remote Help is an Intune-integrated app that lets a help desk technician take control of, or simply view, a managed user's remote device screen to assist with troubleshooting, with the helper's permissions, like full control versus view only, governed by Intune role-based access control (the Remote Help app permissions on an Intune role).
prompt: _____ is an Intune-integrated app that lets a help desk technician take control of, or simply view, a managed user's remote device screen to assist with troubleshooting, with the helper's permissions, like full control versus view only, governed by Intune role-based access control (the _____ app permissions on an Intune role).
eg: Remote Help works against both Microsoft Entra joined and hybrid Entra joined Intune-managed devices, and requires the technician and the end user both to sign in with Microsoft Entra accounts; it needs a Remote Help license, which Microsoft 365 E3/E5 includes from July 2026.

def: The end-user-facing app (Windows, iOS/iPadOS, Android, macOS) where someone enrolls their own device, installs company-published apps, and checks their device's compliance status without contacting IT.
eg: This is the client-side counterpart to a compliance policy's actions for noncompliance: it's where a user actually sees why their device is flagged and what to fix.

term: Win32 app detection rules vs requirement rules
def: A detection rule tells Intune how to determine whether a Win32 app is already successfully installed, such as checking for a file, registry key, or MSI product code, and is mandatory before Intune will report install status. A requirement rule instead gates whether the app is even attempted on a device at all, based on prerequisites like minimum OS version, architecture, or free disk space.
eg: Skipping a detection rule is not allowed for a Win32 app; without one Intune has no way to confirm success, so it will keep reporting the install as pending or failing even after the installer genuinely completed.

def: A supersedence relationship lets a newer Win32 app version automatically upgrade or replace an older deployed version on target devices, optionally uninstalling the old one first. A dependency instead declares that a different app, such as a runtime, must be installed before this app can install, and Intune installs that dependency automatically as part of the deployment.
eg: Dependencies can chain, but a circular dependency between two apps is not allowed and will cause a deployment error, so app packaging needs a strict, one-directional dependency order.

term: Microsoft Store app (new) replacing Microsoft Store for Business
def: Microsoft has retired the Microsoft Store for Business and Education private store; new Microsoft Store app deployments in Intune now source apps directly from the public Microsoft Store using the modern Microsoft Store app (new) type, which supports the same required and available assignment intents without needing a separate business store front end.
eg: Existing line-of-business apps that were side-loaded through the old Store for Business flow needed a migration plan, since simply leaving them in place after retirement does not carry forward new app updates the same way.

term: Apple VPP (Apple Business Manager) app licensing

term: Win32 app install context (system vs user)
def: A Win32 app package can be set to install in the system context, running once for the whole device under SYSTEM regardless of who signs in, or the user context, running separately for each signed-in user; choosing the wrong context for how the installer itself behaves is a common cause of an app that Intune reports as successfully installed but that a specific user never actually sees.
eg: An installer built to write Start menu shortcuts and registry keys per-user will silently fail to register for anyone if it's deployed in system context, even though the install itself and the detection rule behind it both report success.

def: An LOB app uploads a single .msi, .appx, or similar installer file directly to Intune with no packaging step, but supports only basic install/uninstall behavior and a built-in detection method tied to the package itself. term: Automating Intune with the Microsoft Graph PowerShell SDK
def: Nearly every Intune object, including configuration profiles, compliance policies, app assignments, and device actions, is exposed through the Microsoft Graph API, and a PowerShell SDK for it provides cmdlets to script bulk creation, updates, and reporting against those objects instead of clicking through the Intune admin center one object at a time.

term: Custom compliance policies using a discovery script
def: A compliance policy type that runs an administrator-supplied PowerShell script on the device and compares its JSON output against a JSON rules file uploaded with the policy, such as a specific registry value or installed software version, extending compliance checks beyond Intune's built-in, template-based settings.
eg: The discovery script only reports data back to Intune for evaluation; it does not remediate anything itself, unlike a proactive remediation, which pairs a detection script with a separate remediation script.

def: A pair of scripts packaged together and run on a schedule against assigned devices: a detection script identifies a problem, and only if it reports one does the remediation script run automatically to fix it, without waiting for a user to report the issue.

term: Wipe vs Retire vs Fresh Start remote actions
def: Wipe resets a device to factory settings, removing all data, apps, and settings, and can optionally keep it enrolled for reprovisioning. Retire removes only company data, apps, and management from the device while leaving personal data and the OS intact, typically used for BYOD offboarding. Fresh Start reinstalls a clean copy of Windows while optionally keeping user data and Intune enrollment, chiefly to strip out unwanted pre-installed OEM software.
eg: Retire is the correct choice for a personal device enrolled in MDM, since Wipe would destroy the user's own personal data that the organization has no right to remove; a personal device protected only by app protection is not enrolled, so it has no device record to retire and is handled with an app selective wipe instead.
